findings.title: CHECK failure from MakeRef on two-byte single-character string in Maglev constant folding
findings.message: The newly-introduced `GetConstantSingleCharacterStringFromCode` function handles the two-byte (code > 255) case by calling `local_isolate()->factory()->LookupSingleCharacterStringFromCode(code)` and wrapping the result with `MakeRef(broker(), ...)`. However, `MakeRef` requires the object to satisfy broker reference-system invariants (it must be a canonical persistent handle reachable through the broker). A freshly-allocated two-byte single-character string created via the local isolate's factory does not satisfy these invariants, causing a CHECK failure in heap-refs.cc (`Ref construction failed`). This crash is reproducible whenever Maglev constant-folds a string element or `charAt` access that results in a two-byte (non-Latin-1) character, crashing the V8 engine process.
findings.suggestion: For two-byte (non-Latin-1) single-character strings, bail out of constant folding instead of attempting to wrap the factory-allocated string in a heap ref. Return an empty `MaybeReduceResult` (i.e., `{}`) for the two-byte path, as the ref construction infrastructure does not support this allocation pattern.

ground_truth.root_cause: The `GetConstantSingleCharacterStringFromCode` helper introduced in the '[maglev] Inline String.p.charAt' commit assumed that `MakeRef(broker(), factory()->LookupSingleCharacterStringFromCode(code))` was safe for all character codes. However, for code points above `kMaxOneByteCharCode`, `LookupSingleCharacterStringFromCode` allocates a new two-byte string on the local isolate's heap that is not a canonical persistent handle known to the broker, violating the invariant checked inside `MakeRef` / `HeapObjectRef` construction.
